_note: Lander power presets (prompt §5.5; docs/research/power-costs-outcomes.md §1-2). Only sourced values are numbers; everything else is null. basis: sourced | derived | assumption. sources are refs.json keys; sourceIdx points into each preset's sources array. 60_curated.py fills every missing field with {value: null, basis: 'sourced', sourceIdx: null, note: 'unsourced'} and validates.

designLifeHours.note: ISRO: 'One lunar day (~14 Earth days)'; 14 x 24 h

facts.text: Communicates with IDSN and the Pragyan rover; the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter is planned as a contingency link (ISRO).
Lander mass 1752 kg including the 26 kg rover (ISRO).

batteryAh.note: Secondary source (The Week, tier C): 'The capacity of the rover battery is 10 Ampere-hour (Ah).'

designLifeHours.note: ISRO: 'one lunar day, which is equivalent to about 14 Earth days'; 14 x 24 h

arrayPowerW.note: Firefly: solar arrays 'provide up to 400 W' (a maximum, not a typical output)

facts.text: More than 14 days of surface operations (346 hours of daylight), then operated just over 5 hours into the lunar night (Firefly).
Planned: about one lunar day plus several hours into the lunar night (NASA press kit).

designLifeHours.note: NASA press kits: 'approx. 10 days (lunar surface operations)'; 10 x 24 h

facts.text: IM-1 operated on the lunar surface for approximately seven Earth days (NASA IM-2 press kit).
Array power, battery capacity and bus voltage are unsourced: the 200 W / 25 Ah / 28 V figures appear only on Wikipedia, and the NASA press kits give no power specifications.
Power hardware: a lightweight 'SUS laminated battery' and a 'thin-film solar cell' (first adoption in Japan for curved surfaces) (JAXA).
'SLIM was therefore not designed to stay active through the night.' (JAXA)
Array power and battery capacity are unsourced.

batteryAh.note: Descent stage: 5 batteries x 415 Ah (Grumman). Ascent stage adds 2 x 296 Ah.

busV.note: '28 volts dc' nominal, '24 to 32 volts dc' range (Grumman)

batteryWh.note: 5 x 415 Ah x 28 V (descent only); ascent adds about 16.6 kWh

facts.text: Silver-zinc batteries, 20 cells, potassium hydroxide electrolyte (Grumman).
This describes the 5-descent-battery LM of the later J-missions; the Apollo 11 LM battery count is unsourced.

cellEfficiency.note: Triple-junction cell, 29.2% BOL at 1367 W/m2, AM0, 28 °C (AZUR SPACE 3G30-Advanced datasheet). Bare cell; packing and degradation not included.

panelAreaM2.note: Derived: area a 29.2%-efficient array needs to produce 738 W (Chandrayaan-3 Vikram) at 1361 W/m2 and normal incidence: 738 / (1361 x 0.292). Not Vikram's real panel area.

arrayPowerW.note: Team to choose; no published default.

batteryWh.note: Team to choose; no published source for a teaching default.

baseLoadW.note: Team to choose; no lander base load is published in the sources found.

commsLoadW.note: Team to choose; no lander comms load is published in the sources found.

designLifeHours.note: Set by the chosen mission profile.

facts.text: Array power model: P = S(r) x A x eta x cos(incidence) x packing/degradation factor, with S(r) = S0 (1 AU / r)^2 and r from the ephemeris. The packing/degradation factor is a model assumption.
